How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Why Gen Z needs a different approach to education
Article Text:
.

Measure learning through capability

Recognise the individual learner

.

Teach students to think with technology

Develop initiative and global capability

Prepare students to keep learning

This article has been contributed by Dr. Amol Gawande,

Director of Brookstone Institute of Global Studies, Dubai, and an Executive Board Member of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS)

Disclaimer: The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

For generations, education followed a predictable path. Learn what is taught, complete a degree, find a job and build a career. But Gen Z is entering a world where artificial intelligence, automation and evolving skill requirements are reshaping that journey.I believe education must respond by combining strong academic foundations with the ability to apply knowledge in unfamiliar situations.Information is available almost instantly. Students can access lectures, research and practical demonstrations from across the world. The greater educational challenge is helping them interpret that information, question assumptions and use it well. My experience in management education has reinforced a simple principle: students need opportunities to apply, experiment, reflect and improve throughout their studies.Completing a syllabus does not necessarily mean a student can analyse a business problem, communicate an idea or lead a team. We need to judge education by the capabilities students develop, alongside the knowledge they acquire.Outcome-based education provides a framework for this shift. It asks what students should be able to demonstrate after a course, then connects teaching and assessment to those outcomes. In management education, these may include analytical thinking, financial understanding, communication and effective teamwork.I have emphasised internships, corporate interaction and project-based learning throughout my academic leadership. Case studies, simulations and live projects give concepts a practical context. They also allow students to encounter problems without a single textbook answer. Academic rigour becomes more meaningful when students can use it to explain a decision or develop a solution.Students bring different strengths, interests and ambitions to the classroom. Some are drawn to entrepreneurship; others excel in analysis or communication. Many need support in identifying a career direction.Personalised learning does not require a separate curriculum for every student. It requires attention to the individual behind the qualification. Mentoring, career counselling, psychometric assessment and development tailored to a student’s profile can help them understand their strengths and make informed choices. Education should help students explore the professionals they could become, as well as the degrees they can complete.Adding AI or robotics to a curriculum is only a starting point. Students also need to understand how technology affects business models, professional decisions and careers.When a tool generates an answer, the learner must still judge whether the question was useful, the answer is sound and the application is appropriate. Critical thinking, creativity, communication and ethical reasoning therefore belong at the centre of technology education.My experience increasingly intersect with digital transformation and emerging technologies. That experience reinforces my view that technical familiarity must be accompanied by judgement. Students need to understand how to think with technology and use it responsibly.Entrepreneurship education extends beyond starting a company. It develops the habit of identifying problems, testing solutions, accepting uncertainty and creating value. I have advocated for students to become creators of opportunities. That mindset is equally useful within an established organisation, where an employee may spot a problem and develop a better way of working.Global exposure also needs a clear educational purpose. Travel alone cannot create global competence. Students need opportunities to understand different markets, cultures and ways of thinking through exchanges, international collaborations and cross-cultural projects.In my academic leadership experience, international partnerships have created opportunities for student and faculty exchanges, joint programmes and collaborative research. Their educational value lies in helping participants work across differences and apply what they learn in a globally connected environment.A graduate’s first job may not define their eventual career. As industries and roles evolve, the knowledge gained at the beginning of working life will need to be revisited. Education must develop the confidence and habits to learn, unlearn and relearn.This requires classrooms that remain connected to the world outside them. Real business problems, industry interaction and opportunities to experiment should be part of the learning experience. Strong conceptual knowledge provides the foundation; practical experience helps students test and deepen their understanding.I believe educators must ask whether our education systems are ready for the students we teach. Our responsibility is to develop people who can think independently, apply knowledge and continue learning long after graduation. For Gen Z, that is the educational experience we need to build.
Article Summary: For generations, education followed a predictable path. Learn what is taught, complete a degree, find a job and build a career. But Gen Z is entering a world where artificial intelligence, automation and evolving skill requirements are reshaping that journey. Education must respond by combining strong academic foundations with the ability to apply knowledge in unfamiliar situations.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Dreame X60 Ultra Complete robot vacuum cleaner review: Everyday cleaning made super easy
Article Text:
Rating – 4/5

Design and build

Performance

Powerful suction for everyday dirt

Verdict

Robot vacuums are designed to take some of the effort out of everyday cleaning, but can a machine at this price do enough to reduce the need for manual cleaning? Dreame is betting on a combination of powerful suction, AI-powered navigation, hot-water mop cleaning and a slim design that can reach under low furniture. The company recently launched Dreame X60 Ultra Complete in India that an also cross certain raised surfaces that may stop other robot vacuums. At Rs 1,29,999, the Dreame X60 Ultra Complete sits firmly in the premium end of India's robot vacuum cleaner market. While the features sound promising on paper, but the real question is whether they make a noticeable difference in Indian homes, where dust, hair, food spills and different floor surfaces can make daily cleaning challenging. We look at what the Dreame X60 Ultra Complete offers and whether its features justify the premium price.The Dreame X60 Ultra Complete takes a different approach to robot vacuum design, with a slim profile that allows it to reach spaces where bulkier models may struggle. Measuring just 7.95cm in height, it is designed to clean under low furniture, including beds and sofas. Its retractable DToF/LDS navigation sensor helps the robot maintain this low profile, although the stated clearance requirements depend on the navigation mode and the space available under the furniture.The design also focuses on handling obstacles around the home. Dreame's ProLeap system allows the robot to cross single steps up to 4.5cm and double-layer obstacles up to 8.8cm under specified conditions. Its Triple-Wheel AgiLift chassis can handle double-layer thresholds up to 30mm and lift the chassis when moving onto carpets.The robot also features an extendable side brush and mop to reach corners and edges that can be difficult for round robot vacuums to clean. Its base station houses the cleaning and maintenance functions, including automatic dust emptying, mop washing with water heated to up to 100°C under laboratory conditions, and hot-air mop drying. Talking about the base station, it has a premium design with slightly golden finish that fits into modern homes.Dreame X60 Ultra Complete is designed to make everyday cleaning less dependent on human intervention, and that is where it makes a strong impression. The vacuum is efficient, and once the cleaning schedule and settings are configured, it can handle routine cleaning on its own. Its custom cleaning modes are another highlight, particularly the option to select specific zones instead of running the robot across the entire house every time. This is useful for targeting areas that need more frequent cleaning.The robot offers up to 35,000Pa of suction, supported by Dreame's HyperStream Detangling DuoBrush 2.0. The brush combines bristled rubber and TPU rubber rollers to pick up dust and debris from hard floors and carpets. Suction levels can also be adjusted through the app, giving users more control over how the robot cleans different surfaces. In everyday use, the overall cleaning efficiency is a key strength, although the advertised suction figure is based on the company's laboratory tests and does not, by itself, indicate how much dirt will be collected in every situation.The X60 Ultra Complete uses two 120-degree cameras, an LED light and its OmniSight system to identify obstacles and plan its route. Dreame says the system can recognise more than 280 types of objects. This is intended to help the robot navigate around everyday items rather than simply following a fixed cleaning path.One of the more interesting features is proactive illumination dirt detection. The robot uses light to make difficult-to-spot dirt, hair and light-coloured liquid messes easier to identify. It can then adapt its cleaning approach to the area. This is particularly relevant for debris that may not be obvious under normal room lighting.For mopping, the robot uses two rotating pads that spin at up to 230RPM and apply 15N of downward pressure. Dreame's system is designed to tackle everyday marks on hard floors, while the base station washes the mop pads using water heated to up to 100°C under laboratory conditions. The pads are also dried with hot air after cleaning. This automated maintenance is useful as it reduces the need to wash and dry the mop pads manually after every cleaning cycle.The 7.95cm-thin body is designed to reach beneath low furniture, while the retractable navigation sensor helps the robot maintain its low profile. Its extendable side brush and mop can also reach towards corners and edges, areas that round robot vacuums can sometimes miss.For homes with raised thresholds, the ProLeap system is rated to cross single steps up to 4.5cm and double-layer obstacles up to 8.8cm under specified conditions. The chassis can also lift to handle double-layer thresholds up to 30mm and adapt to carpets. These features are intended to reduce the need to move the robot between rooms manually.The all-in-one PowerDock is central to the hands-free experience. It automatically empties the robot's dust box, washes and dries the mop pads, refills the robot's water tank and dispenses cleaning solution. Dreame claims up to 100 days of hands-free dust emptying, depending on usage and conditions.While the dock adds convenience, but it does not eliminate all maintenance. The dust bag, water tanks and other components will still need periodic attention.At Rs 1,29,999, the Dreame X60 Ultra Complete is a premium robot vacuum cleaner that makes a strong case for itself through efficient cleaning and automation. Its powerful suction, custom zone-cleaning modes, slim design and ability to handle certain raised thresholds make it a versatile option for everyday home cleaning. The self-cleaning dock also reduces the effort involved in maintaining the vacuum and mop. However, the high price means it will appeal mainly to buyers who value convenience and want to minimise their involvement in daily cleaning. While it still requires periodic maintenance, its ability to handle routine cleaning with minimal human intervention is a major advantage.
Article Summary: Dreame X60 Ultra Complete is designed to make everyday cleaning less dependent on human intervention. The robot offers up to 35,000Pa of suction, supported by Dreame's HyperStream Detangling DuoBrush 2.0. The base station houses the cleaning and maintenance functions, including automatic dust emptying, mop washing with water heated to up to 100°C under laboratory conditions.

Article Title: WhatsApp brings guest calling, lets people without an account join calls through a link
Article Text:
WhatsApp guest calls support up to 32 people and stay end-to-end encrypted

WhatsApp guest calls keep the host in control

You no longer need WhatsApp to join a WhatsApp call. Meta has started rolling out guest calling, a feature that lets anyone hop on a call through an invite link without downloading the app or signing up for an account.Guests get the same basics that regular users do: free calls, end-to-end encryption and no time limit, so nobody gets cut off mid-conversation. They can also share their computer screen, react with a thumbs up or heart emoji, and raise a hand to speak.There is one catch, and one limitation worth knowing. Only someone with a WhatsApp account can start a call and create the link. Guests can also join from a mobile browser, but they won’t be able to turn on their own camera for now. They can still see other participants’ video during the call.Setting up a call takes a few taps. Open the Calls tab, tap the "+" icon, create a call link and share it with the people you want on the call. Hosts can do this from the phone app or from WhatsApp Web. Guests then type in their name and can join one-on-one or group calls with up to 32 people.Guests can't walk straight into a call. They wait in a waiting room until the host admits them, and the host can remove them at any time.Guests also can't see other participants' phone numbers, send messages or add anyone else to the call.Guest calling builds on web calling, which WhatsApp added in July. That update also brought noise suppression and a way to move an ongoing call between your phone and desktop.Calendar integrations come next. Later this year, users will be able to install a WhatsApp plugin for Google Calendar or Outlook, connect their account and add a call link to their invites. Everyone on the invite can join, whether or not they have WhatsApp.
Article Summary: Meta has started rolling out guest calling, a feature that lets anyone hop on a call through an invite link. Only someone with a WhatsApp account can start a call and create the link. Guests can also join from a mobile browser, but they won't be able to turn on their own camera for now.

Article Title: Google Pay upgrades Flex credit card rewards ahead of festive season; Google One members to get more cashback
Article Text:
Higher rewards on UPI and everyday spending

Additional savings for Google One subscribers

Referral and welcome rewards increased

New Pixel, Fitbit and Google One AI benefits

Google has announced an overhaul of the Google Pay rewards programme for its Flex co-branded credit card, introduced in partnership with Axis Bank and SBI Card, as it looks to attract more users ahead of the festive shopping season. The revised benefits will come into effect from October 16, 2026. Under the updated programme, Google One subscribers will receive significantly higher rewards on everyday spending, while all Flex cardholders will gain access to expanded Google ecosystem benefits, including discounts on Google One AI plans and select Pixel and Fitbit devices.The biggest change is aimed at cardholders who use Flex for regular payments through UPI and other transactions. Google One members holding a Flex credit card will now earn 3.2% back in Stars, with one Star equivalent to ₹1, on all spends during a reward cycle once their total spending exceeds Rs 15,000. Non-Google One members will receive 1.6% back in Stars on all eligible spending after crossing the same ₹15,000 threshold.Google is also introducing category-specific bonuses for Google One members.Eligible users will receive an additional 5% reward on up to Rs 5,000 spent across leading food and grocery applications during each reward cycle.They will also earn an extra 15% reward on up to Rs 3,000 spent on utilities, OTT subscriptions, mobile recharges and related services.The company said these changes are intended to increase value on recurring household and digital-service expenses.Google Pay is also expanding incentives for both new and existing Flex users.The company said it will soon offer Rs 1,000 in rewards for every friend or family member referred to the Flex programme, with no cap on the number of successful referrals.For new applicants, welcome rewards have also been enhanced. Customers applying for a new Flex card can receive welcome benefits worth up to Rs 2,500 within the first 60 days of obtaining the card, depending on the selected card variant.All Flex cardholders will gain access to additional Google ecosystem offers.Starting November 15, 2026, users will be eligible for discounts of up to Rs 3,900 on Google One AI Plus plans, equivalent to a 50% reduction in pricing.Cardholders can also receive discounts of up to Rs 10,000 on the latest Google Pixel smartphones and Fitbit devices purchased from select offline retail stores. Google noted that this offer is currently available only on the Axis Bank variant of the Flex card.
Article Summary: Google Pay overhauls rewards programme for its Flex co-branded credit card. Google One subscribers will receive significantly higher rewards on everyday spending. All Flex cardholders will gain access to expanded Google ecosystem benefits. These include discounts on Google One AI plans and select Pixel and Fitbit devices.

Article Title: OpenAI fires employees after spying device found in office; says: FBI’s investigation is ...
Article Text:
OpenAI: 'FBI's investigation is ongoing'

FBI alleges device targeted confidential AI discussions

Employee arrested, faces prison term

No evidence of leaks so far

OpenAI has terminated an employee after a hidden recording device was discovered inside one of its San Francisco offices, with the company saying it referred the matter to the FBI and is continuing to cooperate with an ongoing investigation. According to a report by Fortune, the federal authorities have arrested 35-year-old Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, an OpenAI engineering lead, on allegations that he secretly installed the device in a conference room used for highly confidential company discussions.The incident came to light on September 30 when OpenAI's technical surveillance countermeasures team found a concealed audio-recording device plugged into a USB port behind a television in a conference room, according to the FBI. The device had allegedly been hidden with a piece of toilet paper and was designed to evade detection, featuring advanced encryption, audio-monitoring capabilities and a mechanism for transferring data.In a statement posted on X, OpenAI said it had used its AI models to analyse the device and trace it back to a specific employee who allegedly planted it days earlier."We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices," the company said."We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier."The company added: "We referred the matter to the FBI, and we're grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI's investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work."OpenAI also stressed that it has found no evidence that sensitive AI assets or customer information were accessed. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," the company said, confirming that the employee had been terminated.According to federal investigators, the conference room regularly hosted discussions involving OpenAI's proprietary research, product plans, business-development opportunities and strategic decisions. The FBI alleged that the device was placed to secretly capture conversations related to the company's advanced AI technologies.FBI Director Kash Patel described the case as a national-security matter. "According to the complaint unsealed today, Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology," Patel said.He added that protecting American artificial intelligence innovation remains a key counterintelligence priority for the bureau.Federal authorities arrested Alfozan on October 9. Prosecutors have charged him with using or attempting to use an electronic device to intercept oral communications. If convicted, he could face up to five years in prison.Authorities allege that OpenAI worked with the FBI between the discovery of the device and the arrest, restricting the employee's access to company systems while investigators gathered evidence. CCTV footage and other evidence reportedly linked him to the device, according to the complaint cited by Fortune.It is unclear what Alfozan planned to do with the recordings. Neither OpenAI nor the FBI has found evidence that anything leaked.“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” OpenAI said in a post on X. The company added that it takes protecting its technology, data and people seriously “as a matter of national importance.” The FBI’s investigation is ongoing.OpenAI said it used its own models to understand the device and to identify which employee planted it. It called the case an example of how AI can help address sophisticated security threats.
Article Summary: OpenAI terminated an employee after a hidden recording device was discovered inside one of its San Francisco offices. The company said it referred the matter to the FBI and is continuing to cooperate with an ongoing investigation. Abdulrahman Alfozan, an OpenAI engineering lead, was arrested on allegations that he secretly installed the device in a conference room used for confidential company discussions.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun opposes Dario Amodei’s call of slowing down AI development, says ‘Anthropic is trying to scare governments by saying…’
Article Text:
Yann LeCun opposes Anthropic: ‘No different from anti-enlightenment’

Yann LeCun, Turing Award winner and widely recognised as one of the three “godfathers of AI,” has pushed back against calls to slow down artificial intelligence (AI) development, accusing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei of using alarmist messaging to lobby regulators and restrict public access to the technology. Speaking during an interview on the morning of October 12 at the Westin Chosun Seoul in Jung-gu, the co-founder and chairman of AMI Labs addressed the intensifying divide across Silicon Valley over safety regulations and model releases.“It’s natural for companies to release products with safety measures to prevent harm to people,” said LeCun, who won the 2018 Turing Award alongside Yoshua Bengio and Geoffrey Hinton for pioneering the foundations of computer vision and image recognition, was in South Korea for the Industrial AI Global Cooperation Meeting ahead of the IIAC 2026 conference in Tokyo.“However, large language models (LLMs) are difficult to fine-tune, so they can potentially harm humans in certain cases. Sam Altman says, ‘We’ll release them cautiously,’ while Dario Amodei argues, ‘They’re too dangerous to manage and shouldn’t be given to the public.’ I oppose Dario’s view,” he added, as per a report in South Korean publication Chosun.LeCun compared attempts to gatekeep underlying model weights to historical efforts to suppress information.“Restricting access is no different from anti-enlightenment – like the Ottoman Empire banning printing in the 15th century to prevent information from reaching people. Ultimately, foundational AI models should be open-source. Only then can human culture, knowledge, and information spread.”When asked whether modern systems can be controlled, LeCun dismissed the notion that today’s large language models pose an existential threat to society. Instead, he framed alarmist narratives as political leverage.“I don’t think current AI is dangerous. The argument for slowing down AI development is a form of marketing or lobbying. Anthropic is portraying AI as extremely dangerous to scare governments. But LLMs aren’t at that level yet.”While talking about the Hugging Face incident, where an OpenAI model attempted to break out of its environment, LeCun argued that such occurrences stem from poor supervision rather than machine malice.“The Hugging Face incident happened due to intentional or incompetent design flaws. Human supervisors failed to properly design the experimental environment, causing AI agents to deviate. Since these agents aren’t inherently malicious, no harm occurred.”Later during the meeting, LeCun reiterated that governing artificial intelligence is fundamentally a technical challenge rather than a crisis of control.
Article Summary: Yann LeCun says Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is using alarmist messaging to lobby regulators and restrict public access to the technology. He was in South Korea for the Industrial AI Global Cooperation Meeting ahead of the IIAC 2026 conference in Tokyo.
